versions.statuteQuote: A tenant who qualifies to terminate such tenant's obligations under a rental agreement pursuant to subsection A shall do so by serving on the landlord a written notice of termination to be effective 28 days after the tenant serves the termination notice on the landlord.

summaryForModel: Under subsection A, a tenant who is a victim of family abuse, sexual abuse or criminal sexual assault, stalking, or trafficking, and who has a protective order or a conviction, warrant, or charge against the perpetrator, may end their obligations under the lease. Under subsection B the tenant gives written notice effective 28 days later, with a copy of the order or charging document. Rent is owed only through that date. A lease that bars this, demands longer notice, or adds other conditions conflicts with this.
paraphraseExamples: Tenant may not terminate this Lease early for any personal reason, including domestic situations.
Early termination requires 60 days' notice and Landlord's written approval in all cases.
tenantExplanation: If you are a victim of family abuse, sexual assault, stalking, or trafficking and have a protective order or a criminal charge against the person, Virginia lets you end your lease with 28 days' written notice.
action: If this applies to you, you can end the lease with written notice and a copy of the order.
